title: DIRECTION- Discontinuation versus contInuation of Riociguat monotherapy in chronic thromboEmbolic pulmonary hypertension suCcessfully Treated wIth balloOn pulmoNary angioplasty
official: DIRECTION- Discontinuation versus continuation of riociguat monotherapy in chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension successfully treated with balloon pulmonary angioplasty
summary: Main objective: To estimate, using a Bayesian analysis, the risk of clinical worsening associated with discontinuation of riociguat monotherapy after successful BPA in CTEPH patients over a follow-up period of at least 12 months, compared with continuation, as assessed by the primary endpoint.
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Signed informed consent and willingness to accept either riociguat monotherapy discontinuation or continuation
2. Adults ≥18 years
3. 3.	Patients diagnosed with inoperable CTEPH or persistent PH after PEA who have achieved therapeutic goals following BPA:  a.	WHO FC I or II  b.	PVR < 3 Wood units  c.	Mean pulmonary artery pressure (mPAP) < 30 mmHg
4. Riociguat monotherapy for ≥6 months with stable doses for ≥3 months prior to enrollment
5. Last BPA session performed ≥6 months prior to enrollment
6. TM6 ≥ 150 m
7. For women of childbearing potential : highly effective contraception
Exclusion criteria:
1. Background treatment with any PH therapy, except for riociguat, (e.g., any endothelin receptor antagonist (ERA), phosphodiesterase-5 inhibitor (PDE-5i), parenteral prostanoids, prostacyclin receptor agonist)
2. Significant obstructive or restrictive lung disease, defined as: FEV₁ < 60% of predicted, with FEV₁/FVC < 65% and/or total lung capacity (TLC) < 60% of predicted, or known significant chronic lung disease diagnosed via imaging (e.g., interstitial lung disease, emphysema)
3. Severe hepatic impairment, defined as: Child-Pugh class B or C and/or liver aminotransferase levels > 3× upper limit of normal (ULN)
4. Severe renal impairment (estimated creatinine clearance ≤ 30 mL/min/1.73 m²)
5. Left heart failure with left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) < 40%
6. Ongoing or planned treatment with organic nitrates.
7. Treatment with strong cytochrome P450 3A4 (CYP3A4) inducers (e.g., rifabutin, rifampicin, carbamazepine, phenobarbital, phenytoin, St. John’s wort)
8. Treatment with strong multi pathway P-glycoprotein (P-gp)/ breast cancer resistance protein (BCRP) inhibitors (e.g., lopinavir/ritonavir).
9. Persons deprived of their liberty by judicial or administrative decision
10. Persons under psychiatric care without their consent, refer to articles L.3212-1, L.3213-1 and L.1121-8 persons admitted to a health or social institution for purposes other than research
11. Adults subject to a legal protection measure (guardianship, curatorship, etc.),
12. Treatment with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor (e.g., ketoconazole, itraconazole, voriconazole, clarithromycin, telithromycin, nefazodone, ritonavir, and saquinavir) or a moderate dual CYP3A4/CYP2C9 inhibitor (e.g., fluconazole, amiodarone) or co-administration of a combination of moderate CYP3A4 and moderate CYP2C9 inhibitors.
13. Persons unable to give their consent
14. Persons who are not affiliated to a social security scheme or who are beneficiaries of such a scheme
15. History of life-threatening hemoptysis (>100 mL within 24 hours) or prior bronchial artery embolization for hemoptysis
16. Pregnancy, breastfeeding, or intention to become pregnant during the study period
17. Severe comorbidities or underlying conditions with an anticipated life expectancy < 12 months, including active malignancy with localized or metastatic disease
18. Alcohol abuse, as determined by the investigator
19. Any condition or factor likely to interfere with protocol compliance, in the opinion of the investigator
20. Participation in another interventional trial or being in the exclusion period following a previous research involving the human person
21. Post-capillary pulmonary hypertension, defined as pulmonary artery wedge pressure (PAWP) > 15 mmHg
